clue.text: Perhaps the purpose of digging a deep hole in the ground is very good, and to be hoped for.

definitions.text: Perhaps the purpose of digging a deep hole in the ground
definitions.note: a deep hole dug in the ground is usually meant to become a well, so its purpose is to be 'well-intended'; 'Perhaps' flags the pun

parts.note: 'well' as an adjective or adverb means good, satisfactory, in fine shape
what is intended is what one plans and hopes for

explanation.surface: A musing on whether digging a deep hole is a good and hopeful project.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a pun: the hole is literally intended to be a well. The answer is written WELL-INTENDED.
explanation.definitionFit: Well-intended means meant kindly; read literally, it describes a hole whose intended outcome is a water well.

clue.text: Rip me up, I see (I hear!)–it's anything but theoretical.

indicators.note: the words are torn up, so their letters are mixed into a new order

parts.note: these two words are taken as written, letters to be torn up and reordered

indicators.note: the speaker hears the phrase, so it is entered as letters that sound the same

parts.note: said aloud, these two words sound like the letters I and C

explanation.surface: A cry of being torn apart, followed by a sardonic remark that it is all very practical.
explanation.definitionFit: Empiric means based on observation and experiment, the opposite of relying on theory.

clue.text: Setting sail is no different, with illicit connections!

indicators.note: setting means arranging, so the letters are put into an order
the letters end up different from how they are written

parts.note: the three words are used as written, letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Going off to sea does not change anything for someone with secret affairs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Setting sail' looks like one phrase about a voyage, but 'Setting' is part of the signal and 'sail' is part of the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A liaison is a secret love affair, here in the plural.

clue.text: Without equal, in April none would be this, when confused.

indicators.note: the two words' letters are jumbled into a new order

parts.note: the two words are used as written, letters to be jumbled

explanation.surface: A puzzling claim that in a month with nothing in it, something would be unequalled.
explanation.definitionFit: A nonpareil is a person or thing having no match, so peerless.

clue.text: Most of December, it might still be glowing.

indicators.note: only the greater part of the month's name is used, dropping its opening letters

parts.note: the month's name is used as written, keeping its last five letters

explanation.surface: A wintry picture of a fire left glowing through December.
explanation.definitionFit: An ember is a piece of coal or wood left smouldering after a fire has died down.

clue.text: It doesn't mean to get out of bed, but you pour cold water on something, if you do.

definitions.text: It doesn't mean to get out of bed
definitions.meaning: first meaning: read as ..., it looks as if it should mean leaving one's bunk, which it doesn't

definitions.text: you pour cold water on something, if you do
definitions.meaning: second meaning: to expose a claim as false, or dismiss it

explanation.walkthrough: The first half is a joke definition: the word is split into a prefix and a word for a bed.
explanation.definitionFit: To debunk is to show up an idea or belief as untrue, which deflates or discourages it.

clue.text: Talk about this! It's what you might hurl to some point.

parts.note: the discus is the heavy disc thrown in athletics
S, for south, is one of the compass points

explanation.surface: An athletics commentator urging us to chat about the throw and how far it went.
explanation.definitionFit: To discuss something is to talk about it with others.

clue.text: Possibly Mae and a Norfolk type, but more likely one from Charleston.

parts.note: Mae West was the Hollywood film star
Norfolk is a city in Virginia, so someone from there is a Virginian

explanation.surface: Speculating whether someone is Mae West or a Virginian, but deciding they come from Charleston.
explanation.walkthrough: Charleston could be South Carolina's city, but it is also the capital of West Virginia, the one meant here.
explanation.definitionFit: Charleston is the state capital of West Virginia, so a resident is a native of that state.

clue.text: How some ramblers go on, stretched to the ultimate.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: people who ramble when talking speak for a long time
second meaning: extended as far as it can go, in full

explanation.walkthrough: Ramblers are walkers too, which makes 'go on' look like a walk, but the sense is a speaker rambling on.
explanation.definitionFit: Speaking at great length means talking for a very long time, in the fullest detail.

clue.text: The former spouse wasn't very good-looking evidently, to show the reason for it.

parts.note: an ex is a former husband or wife
a plain person is not attractive; 'evidently' adds a second hint, since plain also means obvious

explanation.surface: Someone gives a rather cruel reason why their marriage ended: the ex wasn't attractive.
explanation.definitionFit: To explain something is to make clear its cause or account for it.

clue.text: A command to the very young? Stay with the kids!

definitions.text: A command to the very young
definitions.meaning: first meaning: read as two words, '...!', an order given to an infant
second meaning: to look after children while their parents are out

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the whimsical split of the word into an instruction aimed at a baby.
explanation.definitionFit: To babysit is to mind children in their parents' absence, which means staying with them.

clue.text: Words that 10 across school periods.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: words or expressions, especially ones with a set meaning
second meaning: the divisions of the school year

explanation.surface: A reference to the words that account for how the school year is divided.
explanation.walkthrough: '10 across' stands for the answer to that clue, so the clue reads 'Words that explain school periods', linking the two senses.
explanation.definitionFit: A term is both a word with a fixed meaning and one of the parts into which an academic year is split.

clue.text: For a vice president, he didn't leave a good impression–like the auto group started to make Mr. Reagan rub the wrong way. Right?

definitions.text: For a vice president, he didn't leave a good impression

indicators.note: the auto group comes at the start of the answer, before everything else

parts.note: the AAA, or AA, is the motoring association that helps drivers
Ronald Reagan, the president, was known as Ron

indicators.note: the word rub together with the letter from 'Right' are put the wrong way round, out of their written order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A wry remark about an unpopular vice president, with a dig at Reagan being rubbed up the wrong way by a car lobby.
explanation.walkthrough: Aaron Burr, Jefferson's vice president, killed Alexander Hamilton in a duel in 1804 and was later tried for treason.
explanation.definitionFit: Burr was the third US vice president, whose reputation was ruined by the Hamilton duel and treason trial.

clue.text: One wouldn't want to be held this way, as one is being judged.

definitions.text: One wouldn't want to be held this way, as one is being judged.

parts.note: a court can hold someone in a certain state for showing it disrespect, a phrase that also suggests being scorned
the setting is a courtroom, where a judge can impose this finding on someone on trial

explanation.walkthrough: The clue plays on the legal phrase 'held in contempt', which also reads as simply being despised.
explanation.definitionFit: Being found in contempt of court is a penalty for defying or insulting the court during proceedings.

clue.text: Kept something from happening.

parts.note: kept here means stopped or held back, in the past tense
the thing held back is an event, ruled out in advance

explanation.walkthrough: The clue is a plain definition with no wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: To preclude an event is to make it impossible beforehand, preventing it.

clue.text: Badly written so as to make a high point in Greece.

indicators.note: letters that are badly written come out jumbled, so the two short words are rearranged

parts.note: the two words are used as written, letters to be reordered

explanation.surface: Poor penmanship somehow produces a Greek mountain.
explanation.definitionFit: Ossa is a mountain in Thessaly, which the giants of myth piled on Pelion to reach heaven.

clue.text: Sell something, and in Paris one who is often a graduate student, though short, will cause a private fight.

parts.note: to vend is to sell goods
et is French for and

parts.words: one who is often a graduate student, though short
parts.note: TA is short for teaching assistant, a post often held by graduate students

explanation.surface: A trader and a French graduate assistant fall into a personal feud.
explanation.definitionFit: A vendetta is a prolonged feud between people or families, often involving revenge.

clue.text: Chases about aimlessly, with what might help move the cattle.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: ..., as in '... about', roams restlessly in search of pleasure

definitions.text: what might help move the cattle
definitions.meaning: second meaning: spiked rods or goads for driving livestock

explanation.walkthrough: The cattle-prod sense of gad is old and rare; it survives in the word gadfly, the insect that stings cattle.
explanation.definitionFit: Gad as a verb means wander idly; as a noun it is a pointed stick used as a goad.

clue.text: Made of the French type, and bemoaned and denounced the result.

parts.note: de is French for of
cried means wept or lamented

explanation.surface: Someone moaning and condemning the result of something made in French style.
explanation.definitionFit: To decry something is to condemn it publicly as bad or worthless.

clue.text: If you do it while reading a manuscript, you don't like what you see!

definitions.text: If you do it while reading a manuscript, you don't like what you see!

parts.words: If you do it while reading a manuscript
parts.note: an editor goes through a manuscript marking changes with a coloured pencil

parts.words: you don't like what you see
parts.note: the marks strike out or correct the passages the editor objects to

explanation.walkthrough: Editors and censors traditionally used a blue pencil for cuts, so the term came to mean to censor or delete.
explanation.definitionFit: To blue-pencil a text is to edit or cut it, which an editor does to passages they dislike.

clue.text: One who once lived at the mouth of the Columbia River gets to talk in common fashion, with nothing acceptable.

definitions.text: One who once lived at the mouth of the Columbia River

parts.note: chin is slang for chat or talk
O looks like a zero
OK means all right

explanation.surface: A historic Pacific Northwest native is described chatting casually, saying nothing out of place.
explanation.definitionFit: The Chinook people lived around the lower Columbia River in what is now Washington and Oregon.

clue.text: I have found it! It's in California!

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the Greek cry attributed to Archimedes on a discovery
second meaning: a town on California's north coast

explanation.walkthrough: California's state motto is the same word, from the Gold Rush, which links the two senses.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek exclamation for a discovery is also the name of a Californian city.

clue.text: A nightly description.

parts.note: the clue asks for a word that applies to things done at night
the answer is a describing word, an adjective, rather than a thing

explanation.walkthrough: The clue simply asks for an adjective meaning 'of the night'.
explanation.definitionFit: Nocturnal describes animals or activities that are active or happen during the hours of darkness.

clue.text: It ain't true! Possibly soon it will be placed around the junction!

indicators.note: the rearranged word goes round the junction, enclosing it
possibly signals the word could be arranged in another way

parts.note: taken as written, letters to be rearranged
a T-junction, where a road meets another at right angles, is shaped like a T

explanation.surface: A denial, then a hint that something will soon be built round a road junction.
explanation.definitionFit: 'Not so!' is a colloquial denial, saying a claim is false.

clue.text: Condescend, as is shown by wide ignorance.

indicators.note: the answer is on show within the next two words, running across the gap between them

parts.note: the answer runs from the end of the first word into the start of the second

explanation.surface: Being condescending reveals a broad lack of knowledge.
explanation.definitionFit: To deign is to stoop to do something one considers beneath one's dignity.

clue.text: Part of the meal is a green fruit, when the worker is around.

indicators.note: the worker's letters surround the fruit, which sits within them

parts.note: the ant is the classic worker insect in crosswords
a lime is a small green citrus fruit

explanation.surface: A meal includes something green and fruity, served while a worker is nearby.
explanation.definitionFit: Aliment is a formal word for food or nourishment, which is what a meal is made of.

clue.text: Place possibly reminding one of Nathan in the musical.

definitions.text: reminding one of Nathan in the musical
definitions.meaning: second meaning: Nathan ... runs the floating crap game in Guys and Dolls

explanation.walkthrough: Guys and Dolls is the Frank Loesser musical set among New York gamblers; its Nathan bears the city's name as a surname.
explanation.definitionFit: Detroit is a city, so a place, and the surname of a well-known Broadway character.

clue.text: Jewel supports turtles and rattlers!

parts.note: a diamond is a precious gem
to back someone is to support them

explanation.surface: A gem is endorsed by reptiles, an absurd pairing of jewellery and wildlife.
explanation.definitionFit: The diamondback terrapin and the diamondback rattlesnake are both named for the pattern on their skin or shell.
